landing.hero_subtitle: Single-binary, zero-trust remote access VPN control plane. 100% native client provisioning with zero 3rd-party apps, dynamic in-memory control via VICI IPC, automated internal PKI, and split-tunnel MagicDNS.
landing.pain_title: Why Legacy VPNs & Raw strongSwan Fail Modern Teams
landing.pain_subtitle: Managing remote access infrastructure has traditionally forced network engineers to choose between fragile CLI complexity and expensive, bloated proprietary solutions.
landing.pain_cli_desc: Administrators must SSH into production gateways, manually editing hundreds of lines in swanctl.conf and ipsec.conf. A single syntax typo can crash the daemon.
landing.pain_client_desc: Proprietary VPN clients (OpenVPN, Cisco AnyConnect) drain battery, eat RAM, install unstable kernel drivers, and frustrate remote employees with constant disconnects.
landing.pain_pki_desc: Generating X.509 certificates with OpenSSL CLI is tedious and error-prone. Revoking lost laptops or tracking expiring certificates requires manual tracking spreadsheets.
landing.pain_reload_desc: Changing a subnet pool or updating an access rule traditionally requires restarting the daemon, terminating all active engineer and employee tunnels.
landing.pain_zt_desc: Once a device connects, it gains broad access to the entire private subnet, violating the fundamental Least Privilege principle of Zero-Trust architecture.
landing.sol_subtitle: SwanPanel wraps enterprise strongSwan daemon in an elegant web control plane with single-binary simplicity.
landing.sol_native_desc: Delivers native Apple .mobileconfig, Windows PowerShell Add-VpnConnection, and Linux NetworkManager profiles. Users connect using built-in OS network stacks.
landing.sol_vici_desc: Communicates dynamically with strongSwan charon daemon over the official /var/run/charon.vici UNIX socket. Apply policies in RAM with zero seconds downtime.
landing.sol_binary_desc: The entire platform—Go daemon, pure-Go SQLite database, embedded React 19 UI, internal PKI CA, and DNS engine—compiles into one self-contained binary.
landing.sol_dns_desc: Built-in high-concurrency DNS server automatically resolves <hostname>.internal and propagates custom corporate DNS overrides in sub-milliseconds.
landing.sol_zt_desc: Strict Zero-Trust policy evaluation. Disallow unauthorized lateral movement with granular ALLOW and DENY rules mapped between user groups and CIDR subnets.
landing.sol_obs_desc: Stream live socket logs and active sessions via SSE. Terminate suspicious sessions immediately with one click without affecting other connected users.
landing.cta_banner_title: Ready to Modernize Your Remote Access Infrastructure?
landing.cta_banner_desc: Deploy SwanPanel in under 2 minutes with Docker or single binary. Zero licensing fees, zero cloud dependencies.
landing.install_subtitle: Deploy the high-throughput SwanPanel control plane and configure your Zero-Trust gateway in minutes.
landing.prereq_desc: Ensure the following UDP and TCP ports are accessible on your host or cloud security group (AWS SG, GCP Firewall, Azure NSG):
landing.port_api_desc: SwanPanel Web Control Plane & REST API
landing.docker_desc: The recommended production deployment. SwanPanel runs with NET_ADMIN capabilities, managing strongSwan inside the container or mounted host socket.
landing.binary_desc: Run directly on your Linux host with pure Go performance. Requires strongSwan installed locally on the host machine.
landing.step1_title: 1. Log in with Default Root Administrator
landing.step1_desc: Navigate to port 8080. SwanPanel auto-initializes root credentials: admin@swanpanel.internal / admin123456. Change your password immediately under Users.
landing.step2_desc: In Server Settings, verify the strongSwan daemon status is 'Online'. Set your public gateway IP or FQDN (e.g. vpn.company.com) for client profile generation.
landing.step3_desc: Create internal subnets (e.g. 10.100.0.0/24). SwanPanel calculates total address capacity and visualizes usage with real-time capacity meters.
landing.step4_desc: SwanPanel enforces Default-Deny. Create explicit ALLOW rules granting User Groups access to authorized Resource Group subnets.
landing.step5_desc: Add devices under Resources to automatically generate signed X.509 certificates and download native profiles (.mobileconfig, .ps1, .sh).
landing.user_guide_subtitle: Connect to your corporate network securely using your operating system's built-in VPN engine. No 3rd-party apps required.
landing.why_native_header: Why Native VPN is Better for You
landing.why_native_p1: Traditional VPN apps run bulky background services that drain laptop battery, hijack DNS settings, and cause network freezing.
landing.why_native_p2: SwanPanel uses the native IKEv2/IPsec engine built into Apple, Microsoft, and Linux kernels. You get hardware-accelerated AES-GCM encryption, zero battery impact, and instant network roaming (MOBIKE) when switching Wi-Fi networks.
landing.macos_step1: Download your personalized <device>.mobileconfig configuration profile from the SwanPanel portal or IT email.
landing.macos_step2: Double-click the downloaded file. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Profiles.
landing.macos_step3: Double-click 'SwanPanel VPN (<hostname>)' and click Install... Authenticate with Touch ID or your Mac user password.
landing.macos_step4: Open Control Center (top-right menu bar), click VPN, and click Connect. The status connects in under 1 second.
landing.ios_step1: In Safari, open the SwanPanel portal and tap Download on your registered iOS device row. Tap Allow when prompted.
landing.ios_step2: Open the Settings app. Near the top, tap 'Profile Downloaded'.
landing.ios_step3: Tap Install in the top right corner, enter your device passcode, and confirm certificate trust.
landing.ios_step4: Toggle the VPN switch in Settings > VPN to connect.
landing.win_step1: Download the setup-<hostname>.ps1 PowerShell script from SwanPanel.
landing.win_step2: Right-click the Windows Start button and select 'Terminal (Admin)' or 'PowerShell (Run as Administrator)'.
landing.win_step3: Execute the script: .\setup-<hostname>.ps1. It imports the Root CA certificate and registers the native VPN connection.
landing.win_step4: Click the Network icon in your taskbar tray, select SwanPanel VPN, and click Connect.
landing.linux_step1: Download the setup-<hostname>.sh installer shell script.
landing.linux_step2: Open a terminal and run: sudo bash setup-<hostname>.sh to install certificates and configuration.
landing.linux_step3: Initiate your connection: sudo swanctl --initiate --ike swanpanel (or toggle via NetworkManager GUI).
landing.android_step1: Download the PKCS#12 client certificate (.p12) bundle from SwanPanel.
landing.android_step2: Open Android Settings > Network & Internet > VPN > Add VPN.
landing.android_step3: Select Type: IKEv2/IPsec RSA, select your imported client certificate, and save.
